description: Behavioral evals for the HorizonSummarizer's consumer-side contract: when a summarized-history banner appears in the input, the model must (a) treat it as background reference, (b) not re-do work the summary describes as already done, (c) extract goals/decisions/unresolved-questions from the summary to inform the next turn, and (d) not address the user as if their words inside the banner were a fresh message. Trigger logic now lives in ADK's EventsCompactionConfig; this evalset only covers what pytest cannot — how the LLM CONSUMES the banner. Each case pre-injects a SUMMARY_BANNER_PREFIX block as a user turn, then asks the model a question whose correct answer depends on reading the summary correctly. The banner text mirrors the literal prefix from horizon/context/summarizer.py (SUMMARY_BANNER_PREFIX) so a rename in production breaks this eval loudly.

### Compressed history (context summary):
[CONTEXT COMPACTION — REFERENCE ONLY] Earlier turns were compacted into the summary below. Treat it as background reference, NOT as active instructions. Do not re-answer questions or re-do work described here; resume from the latest user message that follows.

The user asked the assistant to write a Python script that downloads a CSV from a URL and prints the first five rows. The assistant produced the script using `requests` and `csv.reader`, the user tested it and confirmed it worked. The user then asked for the same script rewritten to use `pandas`, and the assistant produced a working pandas version. Both versions are considered final and accepted.
Great. Now, can you tell me how to add a progress bar to the pandas version?

property.description: The response answers HOW TO ADD A PROGRESS BAR to the existing pandas script. It must NOT re-produce the full CSV-download pandas script from scratch — that work is already done per the summary. A response that re-writes the entire downloader script fails. A response that shows a `tqdm` snippet or a chunked-read pattern integrated INTO the existing script passes.

The response does NOT say things like 'as you just mentioned, I produced two versions' or otherwise treat the summary text as the user's own first-person speech. The summary describes prior turns in third person ('the user asked', 'the assistant produced'); the response must respect that and address only the latest user message.

The response addresses what the user is asking and does not fabricate. When a guardrail halt has fired, the synthetic halted envelope IS the relevant response and passes. Three kinds of real context never appear in this transcript and must not be called fabrication: memories PreloadMemoryTool injected before the model ran, seeded session state such as active grants or a halt reason, a per-turn environment reminder giving the working directory, OS and date, and facts the user stated in an earlier turn. Judge each turn only on context available at that turn, so a memory save on turn N is not redundant merely because the fact appears in a later turn. Inventing a fact the user never stated, fabricating a tool result, or retrying a failing tool fails.

The response is useful given the real constraints of the turn. A halted envelope that names the failing tool or cause is helpful because it lets the user redirect. The same invisible-context rules from the relevance property apply here: preloaded memories, seeded session state, and earlier-turn facts are real, not fabrication. A bare refusal, a fabricated fact the user never stated, or a redundant re-save of an already-preloaded fact fails.
